intro.title: Welcome to Gartok
body: Gartok is a familiar medieval-fantasy world: many races, magic, ruins, nobles with gold to spend.

The economy has tipped. Delving into ruins, catacombs and wild forests for creatures, artefacts and magic items pays far better than honest work -- so everyone who can hold a weapon is out there, risking their neck.

Adventurers band together in guilds, and the big ones grow into something closer to companies: armed, skilled, ruling whole forests as territory. You are founding one, with a little coin and three recruits -- picked next.

vocation.title: Choose a vocation
body: The trade your guild is founded on: six races and one perk that every member shares, whatever their race.
The draft that follows always holds one candidate of each of those six races. The vocation cannot be changed later; the GUILD tab shows it.

pick.title: Building your guild
body: Nine random candidates: a race, an occupation and 3d6 for each attribute. Click three to keep (click again to put one back), then CONTINUE. Expect to lose some: an early squad is meant to be spent.
Your 3 Commission Tokens call an archetype the pool lacks (Leader, Strong, Tough): pick the archetype, then click the candidate it replaces.

identity.title: Identity and leadership
body: The name and banner colour follow the guild for the whole run.

The leader haggles for the guild and leads any group they stand in. You get one free change later; after that only death replaces them. Each card shows how many people that candidate could recruit as leader: 1 + Charisma modifier + racial level.

combat_lab.title: The combat lab
body: Pick one of the benchmark fights, its level and squad size, and say who plays each side. Player 1 is the guild on the left of the board, Player 2 the opposing side; either can be you or the AI.

Every decision, yours and the AI's, is written to combat_lab/<date>/<name>.jsonl: the whole fight can be rebuilt from that file, and each of your moves carries what the AI would have done in the same spot. That is what the AI will be tuned against.

With two humans the screen hides the board between turns: click when only the next player is looking. Capture the flag: an AI-controlled guild plants its flag by itself, and the opposing flag is always placed for you.

map.title: Your guild
body: Each card on the left is one group of your people. Select a group, then click a place on the map to send it there; the panel on the right lists what it can do where it stands.
There is no turn button: once every group has an order the clock runs by itself, and stops when a group needs you. Everyone eats one food a day -- watch the RATIONS line.
Not sure what to do first? Your objectives are on the next screen.

members.title: Your roster
body: Members are listed by group; click one for their sheet, levels and talents. MANAGE GEAR, at the bottom, opens the selected member's group to move gear between them.
SHARE RATIONS lets group-mates eat from that member's pack. A day unfed: hungry (-2 to attributes). Two: starving (max HP 1). Three: too weak to fight. Four: dead.
Death is permanent; the run ends only when the whole guild is gone.
members.suggestion: The REPUTATIONS tab holds your objectives and what each faction wants.

overview.title: How far the guild reaches
body: Every group takes one slot. Fame -- your reputation with every faction, added up -- opens more. Deeds raise it; nothing lowers it.
A group bigger than its leader can hold starts to fray: each day its weakest member may walk. With a free slot they strike out alone; without one they give 7 days' notice, then leave.

reputations.title: What you're playing for
body: There is no score and no fight you must win. The objectives at the top are small tasks that show you what the guild can do; take them in any order.

Below them, each faction lists its deeds. Reputation only moves when you pull one off -- a one-shot achievement, not a grind -- and it unlocks what the card lists. The Pits and the Bankers are open from day one; the others appear once you walk into their places.

squad.title: Picking who goes
body: Click a card to add or drop a member, up to the cap shown at the top. Anyone too weak from hunger is greyed out.
In the arena you pick a stake first: the entry comes out of the squad's purses, a win pays the purse, and nobody dies. Anywhere else the fight is lethal.

battle.title: Fighting it out
body: Each character has 2 action points a turn. Walking, attacking and most actions cost 1; a weapon action costs 2. Space ends the turn. Click a green cell to walk, a red-outlined foe to target it, and again to attack. The wheel zooms, a right-drag pans.

You see only what the active character's light and senses reach; L shows the whole squad's sight. A foe's ? fields are what you have not read yet: everyone reads a foe on first sight, and Assess (1 point) reads harder.
At 0 HP a character is down, not dead: Stabilize or First Aid them before they bleed out.

loot.title: Splitting the spoils
body: Click an item on the ground, then a survivor, to put it in their pack if it fits their load. TAKE WHAT FITS shares out everything it can; whatever is left when you go stays on the field.
Your own dead are on the field too, with their gear.

report.title: After the fight
body: Who stood, who fell and who put whom down. The bars are XP toward the next level: downing a foe pays combat XP only if it is at or above your combat level.

memorial.title: The fallen
body: Death in Gartok is for good. What they carried may still be on the field.

level_up.title: A new level
body: A new level brings a talent pick: PICK TALENTS spends it now, or later from the roster. A new racial level also rolls one more hit die.

reward.title: The purse
body: The guild has no treasury: money lives on each character. Click who pockets the purse.

market.title: Buying and selling
body: Click a shelf row to put it in the cart and BUY shares it out to whoever has room, or drag a row onto one member. Drag pack items onto the shelf to sell them. The party's purses pay together; leftover coin splits evenly on the way out.

The group leader haggles: Charisma, a shared language and a close alignment lower the price. You sell for roughly half the price, and only up to what the shop can pay (SHOP CAN PAY); a day refills its till a little.

Each shop keeps its own shelf: weapons and metal armour at the Smithy, leather and quivers at the Tannery, bows and wagons at the Carpenter, potions at the Apothecary, raw food at the Farm, beer and jerky at the Tavern, lights, rope and traps at the Market. Any of them buys anything.
market.suggestion: Mark an item to auto-sell from its ... menu: with nothing picked, SELL MARKED sells every marked stack at once.

taverna.title: Recruiting
body: Pick a stranger, then who from the party makes the pitch: Charisma against Charisma, in a language both speak. Each member past the guild's second and each step of alignment apart costs 1. A failed pitch can't be retried by that member until the pool turns over next week.
Each member can sponsor 1 + their Charisma modifier recruits; the guild leader adds their racial level.
STUDY rents a room ($15 a day) to learn a language from a Dictionary, or a spell from its Scroll if the student has that school. PERFORM sends anyone with a Musical Instrument on stage for tips.

hunt.title: Hunting the wilds
body: Pick a shift and head out. A crew of three brings back about 1 kg of Meat per 2 hours, and every hour risks an ambush: a real, lethal fight. Wolves leave Hide, which the Tannery buys.
Win and you can keep hunting or go back with what you have. FORAGE WILDS looks for Red Mushrooms and Fruit instead.

ox_hunt.title: Tracking the ox
body: Pick how many hours of daylight to read the ground: each hour is one Wisdom check by your best tracker. Every trail you find makes the next one 2 harder.

Aurochs runs from anyone near and outpaces you: pin him against the groves, a canyon or the map edge, and bring ranged hands. Every few rounds the herd answers his call. The fight is won when he falls.

bank.title: The strongbox
body: Rent a chest once ($90, 30 kg) and keep what the guild isn't carrying, safe and free. Drag an item onto the chest to store it, or onto a member to take it out.

Copper Coins are $1 and Gold Coins $100, both items in the pack. This is the only place to mint or melt gold: a coin stack's ... menu, $1 per coin each way. Shops spend copper first and break gold only when they must.

level.title: Spending picks
body: Each XP track -- combat, work, magic and racial -- has its own talent tree. A lit node means a pick is waiting there: click it to take it.
Combat XP comes from downing foes at or above your level, magic XP from doing it with magic, work XP from hours worked at a job you haven't outgrown. Racial levels come from the sum of the others.

library.title: The Library Catalog
body: Dictionaries go on sale once the guild has 1 reputation with the scholars, and the shelf grows with it.
Anyone who speaks a tongue can write its dictionary on the WRITE tab, with Paper and Ink. The scholars' "A New Translation" job only takes one the shop doesn't already sell.

group.title: Managing a group's gear
body: Click a member on the left to open their column. Drag items between HAND / OFF HAND / BODY / PACK and between members, or click an item and then where it goes; shift or ctrl picks several. Right-click for a quick "send to..." menu.
The ARTIFACT slot holds one artifact (a Signal Horn, say), which gives its wearer a combat action. The QUESTS tab lists the group's jobs and deadlines.

missions.title: Paid jobs
body: Bring what the giver asks, or do the task, before the deadline. The reward splits evenly across the group when you hand it in; a missed deadline fails the job. Some jobs pay reputation instead of money.
The group leader signs, and the job follows that character, not the group. Progress is on the QUESTS tab (MANAGE GEAR & QUESTS on the map).

trust.title: A test of trust
body: The Bankers hand over a sealed chest to carry to Ledger Hold. Don't lose it, and don't open it.
At Ledger Hold you swap it for a letter of receipt; bring the letter back here to finish the job.

ledger.title: Ledger Hold
body: Whoever carries the Bankers' sealed chest hands it over here for a letter of receipt. Take the letter back to the Bankers in the City to finish the job.

craft.title: Crafting
body: Only recipes someone in the party knows appear. Starting one consumes the materials from every pack in the group (never a padlocked item); then each hour rolls d20 + INT toward the batch. A named tool (a Chisel, say) is not consumed, but some pack must hold it.
WORK makes the whole group wait out the hours. ALONE splits the crafter off into a group of their own (it takes a free slot, and only their pack feeds the craft); merge them back by hand.

Everyone can cook -- Jerky, Roast Meat, Fruit Compote -- at a fire: a field campfire (Flint and Steel, 1 Lumber and 1 Coal, from the map), the Claim's, or the house oven. Jerky keeps 20 days; Meat only 2.

initiation.title: The Initiation
body: A school takes the guild's people once the guild has 2 reputation with it. Reputation is the door, not the price: it is never spent.

BEGIN THE RITE: the member boards at the sanctuary in a group of their own (or the whole group waits, with no free slot) and rolls 1d20 + INT a day toward the school: 180 points for Faith, 90 for Blood, 270 for Nature. Leave and the points are kept.

Faith consumes a Holy Symbol: every Priest carries one, so loot it off a Priest you defeat. Blood first tests the blood for 7 days, and a failed test is final. Board is $3 on a day the boarder has no food. The rite grants the school, not a spell: spells are studied from scrolls.

medic.title: The Medic
body: Pick the patients. The price is the potions, First Aid Kit charges and Antidotes the cure would use, at 70% of the shop price; everyone picked leaves at full HP, cured and unpoisoned. The group pays from its packs, richest first.

The whole group waits out the longest treatment: an hour for wounds, eight for sickness, longer for poison. A treatment over a day is a hospital stay: pick that patient alone and Admit them -- they split off until it ends (or the group waits, with no free slot); merge them back by hand.

property.title: The City house
body: With 4 reputation with the Bankers you can buy a house ($1,440, once). It stores 600 kg, but costs $30 in tax every 7 days.
Miss three payments and the Bankers come to collect: give it back and owe them, or squat and risk the guard.
A house can take an oven ($150) to cook in, and garage bays for wagons and animals.

garage.title: The garage
body: Each bay ($690) keeps one wagon and one animal safe at the house. Park what the group doesn't need on the road; a parked wagon keeps its cargo.
Garaged animals eat from the house stash and the parked cargo, and don't count against the herd limit; with no food they starve. Lose the house and you lose the garage.
The Claim has one too, unlimited, once its garrison opens -- safe only while someone stands guard.

watch.title: Someone has to mind the wagon
body: The wagon can't follow you inside, and is no use on a hunt. Click a member to stay outside with it; one guard is enough, even a lone level 0. Guards stay in the group, they just sit this one out.
Left alone it may be gone when you come back: the place can take it (the Ruins and the Nest, 20%) and the animals may bolt (Donkey 5%, Horse 10%, Ox 15%). Cargo and animals go with it.

claim.title: Claiming the wilds
body: Six stages: scout the land (2 h), clear the creatures there (a fight), fence it (10 Lumber, 8 h), sweep a nearby camp (a fight), then hold it with a garrison for 10 days -- each day a 20% chance of a raid.
Once established, the garrison gathers Lumber each day, or just holds the place and rests. Raids still come.
A campfire (1 Lumber, 1 h, a Wisdom check) cooks while someone is garrisoned; an oven (15 Stone Brick from the Mine, 8 h) cooks for good. Once the garrison opens, the Claim has a garage too.

guard.title: The guard has caught up
body: The City guard has caught members with a rap sheet. You choose for the whole group, and pick who speaks.

Surrender and serve the time, fight the patrol (lethal), or run -- which can get you caught again or ambushed. A bluff or a bribe lets you go but the rap sheet stays; a failed bluff lets the patrol strike first.

dialogue.title: Talk before you fight
body: Foes who can talk say their piece first. Pick who answers: their own Charisma and languages count.

Persuading, bluffing or intimidating needs a language shared with their leader; a bribe comes from the group's purses. Each answer shows its odds, and a closed one says why. A failed bluff or threat gives them the first strike; Attack skips the talk.

prison.title: The prison
body: Pay a prisoner's bail to try recruiting them, the same pitch as the tavern: Charisma against Charisma, +2 for their gratitude.
If the pitch fails they walk free with your money.

stable.title: The stables
body: Animals belong to the group, and their tack decides the job: a Pack Saddle carries cargo, a Harness pulls a wagon. Fit tack here, or drag it onto the animal on the gear screen.
Wagons come from the Carpenter. HITCH an animal in a Harness to a wagon on the gear screen; the wagon carries no more than its animals can draw.
Animals eat a ration a day from the group's food and starve after three unfed days. If the whole group dies, its animals go with it.

wagon_yard.title: The wagon yard
body: A Cart ($150) carries up to 180 kg, a Carriage ($600) up to 540 kg. Cargo never goes into a fight, and the group eats from it on the road. An empty wagon sells back here.
A wagon needs animals in a Harness (the Farm's stables) and carries only what they can draw. If the whole group dies, the wagon goes with it.
The road wears it 1 HP per 100 distance. At 0 HP it breaks: REPAIR it on the group screen (Lumber, 1 h, best INT against DC 15), or leave it behind.

work.title: Day labour
body: Pick a shift (4 to 16 hours) and the whole group works it. Nothing attacks a wage crew, but it pays little.
A worker with their own tool (an Axe at the Lumber Yard, a Pick at the Mine) is paid more and keeps earning work XP past the first level. Each crew card shows the tool and what 16 h pays.
work.suggestion: Work a 16 h shift when the guild runs out of copper; adventure pays better.

gathering.title: Gathering materials
body: Buy the node's licence once and every group of the guild can gather here instead of taking the wage.

Pick a shift (4 to 16 hours); the haul goes into the group's packs: Lumber and Fruit at the Lumber Yard; Stone Brick, Coal, Iron Ore and gems at the Mine. On average it out-earns the wage, but a pack of beasts may find the crew.

group_turn.title: Another group's turn
body: Every group moves on the same clock. When an order runs out, the game turns to that group, which may not be the one you were looking at.
This card says which band, where it stands and what is about to open. GO ON (or Enter) plays its turn; the map comes back after.
group_turn.suggestion: Name your groups (the pencil on the group screen) to tell them apart here.

arena_talk.adelio-small-knife: Another hopeful with a borrowed blade. Go on, everyone wants the belt. Mind your purse on the way down.
arena_talk.ribit: Bufo holds the flag, Peep holds the water, and I hold your attention. Let's see who tires first.
arena_talk.peep: Wade in, wade in. The water's lovely. I'll count the splashes.
